subject: general
question: A train of length 120 m travelling at 60 km/hr crosses another train travelling in the same direction at 24 km/hr in 30 seconds. What is the length (in m) of another train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 60 − 24 = 36 km/hr

Relative speed in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

Total distance (Sum of lengths) = Relative speed × Time = 10 × 30 = 300 m

Length of another train = Total distance − Length of first train = 300 − 120 = 180 m

**∴ Answer = 180**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 120 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 60 km/hr

Speed of second train (S₂) = 24 km/hr

Time taken to cross (T) = 30 seconds

**Formula used:**

Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₁ − S₂

 Train 1 (120 m) 60 km/hr 
• Train 2 (L2 = ?) 24 km/hr 
• 
• Total Relative Distance = 300 m 
 

**Calculations:**

Relative Speed = 60 − 24 = 36 km/hr

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 120 + L₂ = 10 × 30

⇒ 120 + L₂ = 300

⇒ L₂ = 300 − 120

⇒ L₂ = 180 m

**∴ The correct answer is 180 (Option 3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert Speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Stationary Object

If a train crosses a pole or man, distance covered = length of train. If it crosses a platform or bridge, distance = length of train + length of platform.
